items.content: Problem: Incorrectly used a local language model (e.g., Ollama) without verifying its availability in the environment. | How to avoid: Verify the availability of the chosen model and its dependencies in the environment. Prefer models that are already supported or ensure the environment is properly configured.

items.content: Problem: Used a language model during data preparation, which is unnecessary and caused errors. | How to avoid: Separate the data preparation phase from model usage. Only load and preprocess data during this phase, and use the model during the experiment execution phase.

items.content: Problem: Repeated the same approach without adapting when errors occurred, leading to multiple failures. | How to avoid: When an error occurs, evaluate whether the approach needs to be changed. If the same error persists, consider alternative methods or tools.

items.content: Problem: Missing baseline without label noise makes it impossible to assess the impact of noise on models. | How to avoid: Include a baseline condition with 0% label noise and compare the performance drop of each model relative to their clean accuracy.
items.topic: Does label noise hurt logistic regression more than gradient boosting on a small tabular classification dataset?

items.content: Problem: The wrong dataset was used, leading to misleading results and invalid comparisons. | How to avoid: Ensure the dataset used in the code matches the one specified in the plan. Verify the dataset name, size, and structure before proceeding with experiments.
items.topic: Does label noise hurt logistic regression more than gradient boosting on a small tabular classification dataset?

items.content: Problem: Lack of fixed random seed and repeated experiments leads to inconsistent results. | How to avoid: Fix the random seed using np.random.seed() or similar functions and repeat the experiments at least 5 times to ensure reproducibility and statistical validity.
items.topic: Does label noise hurt logistic regression more than gradient boosting on a small tabular classification dataset?

items.content: Problem: No statistical test was performed to validate the conclusion about model robustness. | How to avoid: Perform a paired statistical test (e.g., paired t-test) to compare the performance of models across noise levels and validate the conclusion about robustness.
